questions.question: 79762. Which imaging modality is considered the "gold standard" for evaluating the extent of bony fusion and 3D structural relations in TMJ ankylosis?
questions.option2: Cephalometric radiograph
questions.explain:
The CT scan is the gold standard because it provides precise information regarding the full extent of bony fusion and 3D anatomical relationships essential for surgical planning.
 

​OPG serves as a primary radiograph to show a flattened/absent condyle or sclerotic mass.
 

​Cephalometric radiographs are used primarily to assess the degree of micrognathia and growth deficit.

questions.question: 79761. Which of the following is considered a primary advantage of cyst enucleation compared to marsupialization?
questions.option2: Provides the complete lining for histological examination
questions.option3: Eliminates the risk of inferior alveolar nerve injury completely
questions.option4: Rapid shrinkage of the cavity before surgical intervention
questions.explain:
One of the major advantages of enucleation is that the cyst is removed intact, making the complete lining available for total histological examination to rule out malignancy or specific cyst types.

Additionally, treatment is completed in a single episode. In contrast, marsupialization results in slow shrinkage and does not yield a full intact specimen for biopsy.

questions.question: 79760. During the clinical examination of a large radicular cyst, a characteristic crackling sensation felt on pressure when the overlying bone is reduced to minimal thickness is known as:
questions.option2: Pitting feeling
questions.explain: As a radicular cyst expands slowly and thins the cortical bone, a point is reached where the bone is reduced to "eggshell thickness". Palpation at this stage produces a characteristic crackling sensation (eggshell crackling). When the bone resorbs completely, it leaves a soft, fluctuant, bluish mucosal swelling.

questions.question: 79759. A dentigerous cyst develops by the expansion of which structure and characteristically encloses the crown of an unerupted tooth?
questions.option2: Dental follicle
questions.explain: A dentigerous cyst arises from the expansion/dilatation of the dental follicle and attaches at the neck (cementoenamel junction) of the involved tooth. It encloses the crown of an unerupted tooth, preventing its eruption, and is most frequently associated with unerupted mandibular third molars and maxillary canines.

questions.question: 79758. Regarding Recurrent Aphthous Stomatitis (RAS), which statement is correct?
questions.option1: Ulcers frequently occur on keratinized mucosa such as the hard palate.
questions.option2: Most patients who develop RAS are heavy tobacco smokers
questions.option3: Onset typically peaks in late adulthood or old age.
questions.option4: It is the most common oral mucosal disease, affecting up to 25% of the population.
questions.explain: Recurrent aphthous stomatitis is the most common oral mucosal disease, affecting up to 25% of the population. Onset peaks in adolescence or early adult life. Patients are usually non-smokers, and ulcers almost never occur on keratinized mucosa (with the exception of major aphthae).

questions.question: 79757. Which alkaloid component of the areca nut is responsible for inducing fibroblast proliferation in Oral Submucous Fibrosis (OSMF)?
questions.option2: Arecoline
questions.explain: Arecoline, an active alkaloid component of the areca nut, induces fibroblast proliferation and collagen synthesis, penetrating the oral mucosa to cause progressive cross-linking of collagen fibers. Histologically, the subepithelial connective tissue becomes thickened, hyaline, and avascular.

questions.question: 79756. ​A lesion located specifically in the maxilla anterior to the first molar is characteristically associated with which condition?
questions.option2: Ameloblastoma
questions.explain: Central giant cell granuloma (CGCG) is noted specifically for presenting as a lesion anterior to the 1st molar. Other lesions commonly found in the anterior maxilla include radicular cyst, nasopalatine duct cyst, nasolabial duct cyst, AOT, monostatic fibrous dysplasia, and compound odontoma.

questions.question: 79755. Which radiographic appearance is characteristic of Adenomatoid Odontogenic Tumour (AOT) when calcified material is present within the radiolucency?
questions.option2: Tennis racket appearance
questions.explain:
AOT typically presents as a well-defined unilocular radiolucency containing an impacted tooth. When calcified material is present inside the radiolucency, it gives a characteristic snow-flake appearance.

"Driven snow" appearance is characteristic of Pindborg tumour/CEOT.

questions.question: 79754. Which of the following oral potentially malignant disorders carries the highest risk of malignant transformation?
questions.option2: Erythroplakia
questions.explain: Erythroplakia (and speckled leukoplakia) carries a very high risk of malignant transformation. By contrast, conditions like Lichen planus, Chronic candidosis, and Snuff-dippers' keratosis carry a low risk of malignant change.

questions.question: 79753. Which of the following is classified as a local complication arising specifically from local anesthetic injection techniques?
questions.option2: Vasodepressor syncope
questions.explain:
Complications from local anesthesia are divided into local and systemic complications.

Hematoma, needle breakage, needle-stick injuries, cartridge breakage, and failure to obtain anesthesia are classified as local complications arising directly from injection techniques.

Tissue sloughing arises from the drugs or chemicals used, while syncope and anaphylaxis are systemic complications.

questions.question: 79752. Dissociative anesthesia is produced by which of the following agents?
questions.option2: Thiopentone
questions.explain:
Based on the classification of general anesthesia:​

Dissociative anesthesia: Ketamine

​Induction anesthesia (I.V.): Thiopentone, Methohexitone

​Volatile liquids (Inhalation): Halothane, Isoflurane, Ether

​Others: Propofol, Etomidate
idate

questions.question: 79751. Which cleft lip repair technique utilizes a Z-plasty to lengthen the short medial segment using a triangular flap?
questions.option2: Millard’s rotation-advancement technique
questions.explain: The Tennison-Randall technique is a Z-plasty-based procedure that lengthens the short medial segment using a triangular flap. The Rose-Thompson technique is a straight-line repair, and Millard’s technique uses rotation-advancement.

questions.question: 79750. Secondary alveolar bone grafting for cleft alveolus is typically performed during which stage?
questions.option2: Deciduous dentition period (2–4 years)
questions.explain: Secondary alveolar bone grafting is typically performed during the mixed dentition period at 8–11 years of age, before the eruption of the permanent canine. Autogenous iliac crest cancellous bone is commonly used as the graft source.

questions.question: 79749. Which of the following statements correctly contrasts the properties of Dental Amalgam and Composite Resin?
questions.option1: Amalgam undergoes polymerization shrinkage, while composite undergoes galvanic corrosion.
questions.option2: Composite relies on mechanical retention only, whereas amalgam relies on adhesive bonding.
questions.option3: Amalgam shows slight expansion on setting, while composite exhibits polymerization shrinkage.
questions.option4: Amalgam is highly technique-sensitive to moisture, whereas composite is moisture-tolerant.
questions.explain:
Amalgam: Sets via an amalgamation reaction , exhibits slight expansion (providing a favorable seal), is tolerant to moisture, retains mechanically, and can undergo galvanic corrosion.

​Composite Resin: Sets via free-radical addition polymerization, exhibits polymerization shrinkage (unfavorable, C-factor), bonding is adhesive (etch + bond), and is highly technique-sensitive to moisture.
.

questions.question: 79748. Which type of composite resin is specifically indicated for Class V cervical lesions subjected to flexing stresses, mini cavities, and repair of composite restorations?
questions.option2: Flowable Hybrids
questions.explain:
​Flowable Hybrids: Lower viscosity allows them to adapt well to mini cavities, serve as a first layer in multi-layered restorations, repair existing composite restorations, and flex with Class V cervical lesions under abfraction stresses.

​Packable Hybrids: Designed for Class II cavities requiring greater packability to establish tight contact points with adjacent teeth.

​Microfilled Composites: Recommended for low-stress areas and sites requiring high polish (e.g., subgingival Class V lesions) to minimize plaque accumulation.
on.

questions.question: 79747. Compomers (Polyacid-modified composite resins) are suitable for which of the following clinical applications?
questions.option2: Restorative materials in pedodontics and Class V non-stress bearing lesions
questions.option3: Long-term primary impression trays for edentulous arches
questions.option4: Root canal obturation in mature permanent teeth
questions.explain:
Compomers include restorative materials in pedodontics (biocompatible with pulp), non-stress bearing areas, Class V lesions, bases, and luting.
 

Compomers have lower mechanical strength than traditional composites, making them unsuitable for high-stress bearing areas.

questions.question: 79746. What is the specific role of Tartaric acid when added to the polyacrylic acid liquid of Glass Ionomer Cement?
questions.option1: Serves as the primary constituent for silica glass powder
questions.option2: Acts as an inert pigment to provide radiopacity
questions.option3: Improves handling characteristics by increasing working time and shortening setting time
questions.option4: Inhibits the fluoride release in pedodontics
questions.explain:
Tartaric acid functions to improve handling characteristics (increases working time and shortens setting time).
 

​Silica constitutes 41.9% of the GIC powder component, not the liquid.
 

​Radiopacity is provided by agents like calcium tungstate or barium sulphate in paste formulations.
 

Fluoride release is an intrinsic advantage of GIC and Compomers, which Tartaric acid does not inhibit.

questions.question: 79745. According to the ISO classification, which category does Zinc Oxide Eugenol (ZOE) cement belong to?
questions.option2: Oil-based cements
questions.explain:
ISO classification categorizes ZOE and non-eugenol cements as oil-based cements.
 

Water-based cements include Zinc phosphate, Glass ionomer, and Zinc polycarboxylate.
 

Resin or polymer-based cements include resin cements, compomers, and modified polymers.

questions.question: 79744. What is the principal constituent in the powder component of Zinc Phosphate cement?
questions.option2: Phosphoric acid (38.2%)
questions.explain:
The composition table shows that Zinc oxide makes up 90.2% by weight of the powder and serves as its principal constituent.
 

Magnesium oxide (8.2%) is present in the powder, but its function is to aid in sintering.
 

​Phosphoric acid (38.2%) is the principal reactive ingredient in the liquid component, not the powder.
 

Silica (1.4%) acts as a filler and aids in sintering within the powder mixture.

questions.question: 79743. Which of the following statements regarding the ideal requirements of inlay casting wax during the burnout process is correct?
questions.option1: It should leave a thin layer of carbon residue to act as a lubricant.
questions.option2: During burnout at 500 °C, it should vaporize completely without leaving any residue.
questions.option3: It must chip and flake easily to facilitate removal from the die margin.
questions.option4: It should crumble when softened to allow proper adaptation to prepared cavity walls.
questions.explain:
During burnout at 500 °C, the wax should vaporize completely without residue to ensure a clean mold cavity for metal casting.
 

​ Any residue left behind during burnout will contaminate the mold cavity and cause defects in the final metal casting.
 

​when softened, the wax should not flake or crumble , and it should not chip, flake, or tear during carving

questions.question: 79742. Which outcome occurs specifically as a result of over-mixing alginate impression material?
questions.option1: Inadequate wetting and lack of homogeneity
questions.option2: The mix becomes grainy with poor recording of detail
questions.option3: Reduction in working time and destruction of gel fibrils
questions.explain:
Over-mixing breaks/destroys the gel fibrils as they form, leading to a reduction in final strength and a reduction in working time.
 

​ under-mixing results  inadequate wetting, lack of homogeneity, a grainy mix, and poor detail reproduction.
 

 Over-mixing reduces strength rather than increasing it.

questions.question: 79741. Which of the following statements regarding Agar hydrocolloid is correct?
questions.option1: Its setting time ranges between 7 to 15 minutes.
questions.option2: Imbibition causes fluid to exude from the gel onto the surface.
questions.option3: It can be reused as an impression material in the patient's mouth safely.
questions.option4: Reusing agar as an impression material is not recommended due to difficulty in sterilization.
questions.explain:
setting time is about 5 minutes.
 

​ The exuding of fluid from the gel is known as syneresis, which forms small droplets on the surface. Imbibition refers to the absorption/gain of water.

While agar can be reused as a duplicating material in the lab, it is not recommended to be reused as an impression material in the mouth.

questions.question: 79740. A clinician requires a mucostatic (passive) impression for a patient. Which material is most appropriate?
questions.option2: Zinc oxide-eugenol
questions.explain:
Mucostatic (passive) impression materials record oral tissues in their resting state without displacing soft tissue.
Examples include Plaster of Paris, Zinc oxide-eugenol, low viscosity alginates, and low viscosity elastomeric materials.​

Impression compound, high viscosity alginates, and high viscosity elastomers exert pressure and displace tissues, making them mucocompressive.
.

questions.question: 79739. Which of the following features is not an ideal requirement for an orthodontic appliance?
questions.option1: It should be inert to oral secretions, tasteless, and odorless
questions.option2: It should be heavy and bulky to maximize anchorage force
questions.option3: It must exert the correct force in the correct direction
questions.option4: It should be easy to keep clean and repairable
questions.explain:
Ideal Requirements:
#​Must be simple in design and comfortable to use.

​#Should not be heavy or bulky, but strong enough not to break during functional activities like speech, swallowing, and mastication.

​#Must be chemically inert to oral secretions, tasteless, and odorless.

#​Must not cause damage to teeth or surrounding soft tissues.

#​Must exert the correct force magnitude and direction for desired movement.

​#Should be easy to insert, remove, clean, and repair.
d repair.

questions.question: 79738. The functional regulator of Fränkel is classified as which type of functional appliance?
questions.option2: Tooth-borne active appliance
questions.explain:
Tissue-Borne Appliances: These appliances are located primarily in the oral vestibule and have little to no contact with the dentition. The classic example is the Fränkel functional regulator.
 

​Mechanism: By shielding the teeth from the muscular pressure of the lips and cheeks, tissue-borne appliances allow apical base development and dental expansion.

questions.question: 79737. Which appliance is suitable for the management of a developing anterior crossbite?
questions.option2: Sved bite plane
questions.explain:
Developing Crossbite: Early interception can be performed using simple modalities such as tongue blade therapy, lower inclined planes, or placing a metallic crown on an upper incisor tooth.
​Established Anterior Crossbite: Once fully developed, treatment requires active tooth-moving appliances like a double cantilever spring with a posterior bite plane or expansion screws.

questions.question: 79736. Which of the following conditions is considered a CONTRAINDICATION for performing proximal stripping
questions.option1: Mild tooth material excess (0-2.5mm) based on Bolton's analysis
questions.option2: Need to improve arch stability by broadening the contact area
questions.option3: Young patients with large pulp chambers
questions.option4: Discrepancy in tooth sizes preventing Class I canine relationship
questions.explain:
Proximal stripping is contraindicated in young patients because they possess larger pulp chambers, which significantly increases the risk of accidental pulpal exposure or post-procedure dentinal hypersensitivity. Other contraindications include high caries index, enamel hypoplasia, poor oral hygiene, and refusal of consent.

Broadening narrow contact areas into broader contact areas to stabilize rotations and prevent relapse is an established advantage/indication of stripping.
 

 Correcting minor tooth size discrepancies to achieve a Class I molar and canine relationship is an indication for reproximation.

questions.question: 79735. Which of the following is considered a DISADVANTAGE of fixed space maintainers?
questions.option1: Interference with the passive eruption of abutment teeth
questions.option2: Decalcification of tooth material under the bands
questions.option3: Restricting natural jaw growth in pediatric patients
questions.option4: Inability to be used in uncooperative pediatric patients
questions.explain:
A key disadvantage of fixed space maintainers is that enamel decalcification of tooth material can occur under the bands if oral hygiene is poor or cement dissolves.

Other disadvantages include requiring elaborate instrumentation/expert skill and potential supra-eruption of opposing teeth if pontics aren't placed.

questions.question: 79734. Which of the following conditions is not a recognized cause of Pseudo Class III (postural/habitual) malocclusion?
questions.option1: Presence of occlusal prematurity deflecting the mandible forward
questions.option2: Premature loss of primary posterior teeth causing forward movement of the mandible
questions.option3: Enlarged adenoids prompting forward posture of the mandible to clear the airway
questions.option4: Genetically determined excessive growth of the mandible
questions.explain:
An excessively large mandible due to genetic origin is a cause of True Class III / Skeletal Class III malocclusion, not Pseudo Class III.

 Occlusal prematurity is a key etiology of Pseudo Class III because it causes functional deflection of the mandible anteriorly upon closure.

Early loss of primary molars forces the child to position the mandible forward to establish anterior occlusal contact.

​Enlarged adenoids force the child to position the mandible forward and lower the tongue to prevent it from contacting the adenoids and obstructing the airway.

questions.question: 79733. Which of the following is an example of a Primary Motive?
questions.option2: Reward
questions.explain:
Motivation is classified into two main types:​
Primary motives: Inborn desires that initiate people to take action, such as hunger, survival, sex, etc.

​Secondary motives: Desires caused by external forces or incentives, such as praise, love, reward, or punishment.
nt.

questions.question: 79732. The word "Communication" is derived from which Latin word, and what does it mean?
questions.option2: "Commune", meaning common understanding
questions.explain: The word communication is derived from the Latin word "commune", which means common understanding.

questions.question: 79731. Which of the following is explicitly listed as a purpose of planning?
questions.option1: To eliminate wasteful expenditure and duplication of effort
questions.option2: To replace private dental practices with state-run facilities
questions.option3: To bypass political considerations in health administration
questions.option4: To shorten the clinical training required for dental practitioners
questions.explain:
Main purposes of planning:
​To match limited resources with many problems.

​To eliminate wasteful expenditure and duplication of expenditure/effort.

​To develop the best course of action to accomplish a defined objective.

questions.question: 79730. Which technique is categorized as an "Advanced Behavior Guidance Technique"?
questions.option2: Aversive conditioning techniques (e.g., HOME, Implosion therapy
questions.explain:
Advanced Behavior Guidance Techniques:
Protective stabilization, Sedation, and General anesthesia.

questions.question: 79729. Which of the following is a primary use of Biostatistics as outlined in public health?
questions.option1: Defining the natural history and causation of disease
questions.option2: Evaluating the efficacy of vaccines by controlled studies
questions.option3: Studying patterned human relationships in social groups
questions.option4: Formulating the "conversion mechanism" for health care resource management
questions.explain: Biostatistics is utilized to test whether differences between populations are due to chance, define normalcy, evaluate vaccine efficacy through controlled trials, measure morbidity/mortality rates, and assess public health program progress.

questions.question: 79728. Which of the following is classified as an "Interdental oral hygiene aid" under Mechanical Plaque Control?
questions.option2: Single tuft brushes
questions.explain: Interdental oral hygiene aids include Dental floss, Dental floss holder, Toothpicks and Toothpick Holder, Interproximal brushes, Single tuft brushes, Knitting yarn, Gauze strip, Pipe cleaner, and Wedge stimulator

questions.question: 79727. Which surface of a complete denture is also referred to as the "Intaglio surface"?
questions.option2: Occlusal surface
questions.explain:
Impression surface (Intaglio surface): The tissue-bearing inner portion of the denture that directly contacts the oral mucosa.

​Polished surface (Cameo surface): The exterior non-articulating surface bounded by the borders and occlusal plane.

​Occlusal surface: The surfaces of the artificial teeth that make contact with opposing teeth.
eeth.

questions.question: 79726. Where is the Postpalatal Seal region located anatomically?
questions.option2: Extends between the two maxillary tuberosities
questions.option4: Along the anterior third of the hard palate
questions.explain:
The posterior palatal seal area is divided into two distinct regions based on anatomical landmarks: the pterygomaxillary seal and the postpalatal seal. The postpalatal seal is defined as the part of the posterior palatal seal that extends between the two maxillary tuberosities.
 

 The fovea palatina are mucous gland duct openings used as an arbitrary landmark, not the entire postpalatal seal region.

The seal is located at or along the junction of the hard and soft palates.

questions.question: 79725. n which clinical scenario is a Bar Clasp contraindicated
questions.option2: When the retentive undercut is on the gingival third
questions.option3: Tilted abutment teeth with soft tissue undercuts
questions.explain:
A bar clasp approaches the tooth from the gingival aspect across the tissue. If severe soft tissue undercuts or severe tooth tilting exist, the bar clasp approach arm can impinge on tissue or trap food, making it contraindicated. In such cases, a circumferential clasp is preferred.
 

​Bar clasps are suitable or preferred for aesthetic areas (e.g., premolars) where gingival undercuts exist without severe soft tissue impingements.

questions.question: 79724. Definitive management of an alveolar cleft patent usually involves which of the following treatment protocols?
questions.option1: Continuous use of an interim obturator throughout life
questions.option2: Bone grafting in the defective area followed by a fixed implant prosthesis
questions.option3: Placement of a meatal obturator using silicone elastomers
questions.option4: Application of a treatment prosthesis without surgical intervention
questions.explain:
Management of patient with alveolar cleft:
​Temporary management: The condition can be managed temporarily using a removable partial denture.

​Definitive management: Involves surgical intervention via bone grafting in the defective area followed by a fixed implant prosthesis.
.

questions.question: 79723. Which part of a bridge directly replaces the missing natural tooth or teeth?
questions.option2: Connector
questions.explain:
Pontic: The artificial tooth that replaces the missing natural tooth or teeth in a fixed partial denture.
 

​Retainer: The portion of a fixed bridge that is cemented onto the prepared abutment tooth.
 

​Connector: The part that unites the pontic to the retainer.
 

​Abutment: The natural tooth or root that serves to support and retain the bridge.

questions.question: 79722. ​What role does Carbopol play in carbamide peroxide bleaching gel formulations?
questions.option1: Serves as a primary oxidizing agent that reacts with chromophores
questions.option2: Acts as a thickening agent to prolong the release of active peroxide
questions.option3: Prevents tooth sensitivity by occluding exposed dentinal tubules
questions.option4: Acts as a solvent to rapidly breakdown carbamide peroxide into urea
questions.explain:
Carbopol (a polyacrylic acid polymer) is added to carbamide peroxide bleaching gels as a thickening agent.
 

​It increases viscosity and slows down the degradation rate, thereby prolonging the sustained release of active peroxide during bleaching.
 

​Carbamide peroxide decomposes into urea, ammonia, carbon dioxide, and hydrogen peroxide during the bleaching process.

questions.question: 79721. Which of the following is a major clinical advantage of nanofill and nanohybrid composite resins?
questions.option1: Exceptionally high polishability with tooth-like translucency
questions.option2: Requirement of a single-step bulk curing under UV light
questions.option3: Complete absence of organic resin matrix
questions.option4: Susceptibility to surface gloss loss from tooth brushing
questions.explain:
Nanofill & Nanohybrid Composites: Feature average particle sizes smaller than traditional microfilled composites, giving them high polishability, optimal mechanical properties, and excellent aesthetic translucency.
 

​They are suitable for both anterior and posterior restorations due to high wear resistance and good handling characteristics.

questions.question: 79720. Which mechanism of adhesion primary involves the penetration of resin into tooth structure to form resin tags?
questions.option2: Micromechanical
questions.explain:
Micromechanical bonding occurs when a material penetrates into another structure at a microscopic level, such as resin infiltrating micropores to form resin tags within the tooth structure.
 

​Adsorption involves chemical bonding to organic or inorganic components of the tooth.
 

​Diffusion involves the precipitation of a substance on the tooth surface to which resin monomers bond mechanically or chemically.

questions.question: 79719. Which of the following interventions INCREASES the tissue-dissolving efficacy of Sodium Hypochlorite?
questions.option2: Increasing contact time within the root canal
questions.explain:
Factors that increase NaOCl efficacy include:

​Increasing the volume of the solution.

​Heating the solution to 60-70°C
​Increasing the contact time inside the root canal system.

​Ultrasonic activation.

​Buffering with 1% sodium bicarbonate.

​Conversely, longer storage time and addition of chelating agents (like EDTA) decrease NaOCl efficacy.

questions.question: 79718. What is the major limitation of Normal Saline when used as a root canal irrigant?
questions.option1: It causes severe periapical tissue damage upon extrusion
questions.option2: It lacks antimicrobial activity, tissue dissolution, and smear layer removal properties
questions.option3: It reacts violently when mixed with EDTA
questions.option4: It has an osmotic pressure drastically different from blood
questions.explain:
Normal saline is highly biocompatible and causes no adverse periapical reaction because its osmotic pressure matches that of blood.
 

​Its major disadvantages are that it does not possess tissue-dissolving or disinfecting properties, lacks antimicrobial action, cannot clear microbial flora from inaccessible regions (e.g., accessory canals), and does not remove the smear layer.

questions.question: 79717. An Electronic Apex Locator (EAL) is particularly advantageous over conventional radiographs in which of the following anatomical or clinical scenarios?
questions.option1: Superimposition of the zygomatic arch over root apices
questions.option2: Presence of tori or excessive bone density
questions.option3: Impacted teeth or shallow palatal vault
questions.explain:
Radiographs often suffer from anatomical superimposition (such as the zygomatic arch or excessive bone density) and difficulty in film placement due to a shallow palatal vault or gag reflex.
 

​EALs provide objective length determination without radiation interference in conditions where the apical portion of the canal is obscured by impacted teeth, zygomatic arch, tori, excessive bone density, overlapping roots, or a shallow palatal vault.

questions.question: 79716. C-shaped root canal configuration is most commonly encountered in which of the following teeth?
questions.option2: Maxillary premolars
questions.explain:
C-shaped canals feature a single ribbon-shaped pulp chamber with a 180°arc or more and are usually found in mandibular molars.
 

​Apical curves are commonly seen in maxillary lateral incisors and the mesiobuccal root of maxillary molars.
 

​Bayonet-shaped canals are typically observed in premolars.

questions.question: 79715. Which of the following is considered a DISADVANTAGE of the bisecting angle radiographic technique?
questions.option1: Inability to perform without a film holder
questions.option2: Increased discomfort when a rubber dam is placed
questions.option4: High failure rate in patients with shallow palatal vaults
questions.explain:
Disadvantages of Bisecting Angle Technique:​
Image distortion (dimensional inaccuracy due to angulation).
​Cone cutting.

​Superimposition of adjacent anatomical structures (e.g., zygomatic arch over maxillary molar roots).

​Difficulty in reproducing identical alignment on follow-up films because a film holder with an aiming device is omitted.
tted.

​Advantages: It is comfortable, quick, easily adaptable when a rubber dam is in place, and does not strictly require a film holder.

questions.question: 79714. What is a "Phoenix Abscess"?
questions.option1: An acute periodontal infection secondary to deep pocketing
questions.option2: An acute inflammatory reaction superimposed on a pre-existing chronic periapical lesion
questions.option3: A chronic sinus tract draining an asymptomatic periapical cyst
questions.option4: Reversible pulp inflammation following dental restoration
questions.explain:
A Phoenix Abscess (also known as a recrudescent abscess or acute exacerbation of asymptomatic apical periodontitis) develops when an existing chronic periapical lesion—such as a periapical granuloma or cyst—suddenly undergoes an acute inflammatory response.
 

​Clinically, it presents with acute abscess symptoms (pain, swelling, tenderness to percussion) superimposed on radiographically evident pre-existing chronic bone loss.

questions.question: 79713. Which of the following is a recognized DISADVANTAGE of pin-retained restorations?
questions.option1: Requires at least two clinical appointments
questions.option2: Decreases the tensile and transverse strength of amalgam
questions.option3: High cost compared to cast restorations
questions.option4: Requires excessive removal of sound tooth material
questions.explain:
Disadvantages of Pin Restorations:​*Pins do not increase the compressive strength of amalgam and actually decrease its tensile and transverse strength.
​* They introduce stresses in dentin (craze lines or cracks).
​* Risk of pulpal exposure or external tooth perforation if drilled in the wrong direction.
​* Potential microleakage if the pin end appears near the restoration surface.

​Advantages:
Pin restorations are more conservative of tooth material than cast preparations, require only one appointment, and are inexpensive compared to cast restorations.
